**Summary:** Across 300 games you scored 50% against 49% expected [F1], and you made 0.97 times the blunders expected for your positions [F2]. No clear weakness shows up, so this plan is about polishing your play rather than fixing a hole.

## Biggest weaknesses

The evidence here is thin. No opening family shows a clear weakness once rating, sample size and the number of openings checked are taken into account [F8]. Your overall blunder count is not different from expected (interval 0.91 to 1.04) [F2]. Two things are worth watching, but neither has been shown to be a weakness:

1. **Middlegame volatility (not a confirmed weakness).** You blunder on 6.6% of middlegame moves, against 6.5% for your opponents [F10]. That is level with them, but it is the phase where you blunder most often. Your costliest mistakes include 38...Qh2+, which lost 88 win% when Bf6 was better [F16] (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186706648876). *What to do:* before any check or capture, look for every reply your opponent has, then drill the [middlegame theme](https://lichess.org/training/middlegame) [F17].
2. **Occasional big lapses in calm positions (not a confirmed weakness).** When you have over 30% of your clock left, you blunder at 1.03 times expected (interval 0.95 to 1.12) [F5]. That interval does not rule out a normal rate, so it is not a proven problem. Still, 7...h5 lost 89 win% when Nxg4 was available [F15] (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186801191354). *What to do:* when you have time, do a quick "what's hanging?" check before each move, and practise the [hanging piece theme](https://lichess.org/training/hangingPiece) [F18].

## What's working

- **Playing under time pressure.** With under 10% of your clock left you made 0.83 times the expected blunders (interval 0.68 to 1.01) [F3]. With 10-30% left it was 0.82 times (interval 0.66 to 1.01) [F4]. Neither interval clearly rules out a normal rate, so this is a good sign rather than a proven strength.
- **Your White openings.** In the Queen's Gambit you scored 57% against 50% expected over 51 games [F7], with a median eval of +0.9 after move 12 [F13]. In the Benoni you scored 70% against 49% expected [F6]. Both are rated "possible strength."

## Training plan

- Do [middlegame puzzles](https://lichess.org/training/middlegame) every day [F17], focusing on checking all of your opponent's replies.
- Do a short set of [hanging piece puzzles](https://lichess.org/training/hangingPiece) [F18] before you play.
- Go back over the 43...Kh7 game, where Qxf4+ was better (https://www.chess.com/game/live/186801649660) [F14], and the two games linked above. For each one, write down what you missed.
- Keep playing the Queen's Gambit [F7]. Review how you play moves 13-25, where you lose 5.1 win% per move, the same as your overall average [F13]. Turning your early edge into wins is where you can improve most.
